WJP ggplot2 Theme

Source: R/utils.R
WJP_theme.Rd

WJP_theme() returns a ggplot2 theme object that applies the World Justice Project visual style guidelines to charts.

Usage

WJP_theme(
  family = wjp_font_family(),
  base_size = 10,
  text_colour = "#524F4C",
  grid = c("major", "x", "y", "none"),
  grid_colour = "#5e5c5a",
  grid_linetype = "dashed",
  base_theme = NULL
)

Arguments

family

String. Font family for all text elements. Default is the active WJP font family (see wjp_font_family()), which is "Lato Full" unless changed via options(wjpr.family = ).

base_size

Numeric. Size of the axis text and titles, in points. Default is 10.

text_colour

String. Color of the axis text and titles. Default is "#524F4C". WJP country reports use "#1A1A1A".

grid

String. Major grid lines to draw: "major" (both directions, default), "x" (lines at the breaks of the x scale), "y" (lines at the breaks of the y scale), or "none".

grid_colour

String. Color of the grid lines. Default is "#5e5c5a".

grid_linetype

Line type of the grid lines. Default is "dashed".

base_theme

A complete ggplot2 theme to start from (e.g., ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11)). Default is NULL (a partial theme).

Value

A ggplot2 theme object that can be added to any ggplot.

Details

The theme includes the following style specifications:

  • Transparent panel and plot backgrounds

  • Dashed grey grid lines (#5e5c5a)

  • WJP font family for all text elements (Lato Full by default; see wjp_font_family()). The family is also set on the root text element, so titles, legends, and strips inherit it.

  • Axis text and titles of base_size points in #524F4C

  • No axis ticks

  • Zero plot margins

WJP_theme() is a partial theme: it is added on top of the active complete theme (ggplot2's ggplot2::theme_grey() unless you set another one). Use base_theme to start from a different complete theme, such as ggplot2::theme_minimal().

When passed as the ptheme argument of a WJPr chart function, the elements that differ from the default WJP_theme() are applied after the chart's own styling, so they take precedence (for example, WJP_theme(base_size = 9) resizes the axis labels of every chart). Complete themes (including those built with base_theme) are used as the starting point of the chart instead.

Examples

library(ggplot2)

# Load fonts first
wjp_fonts()

# Apply WJP theme to a plot
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = wt)) +
  geom_point() +
  WJP_theme()


# Same plot with Inter Tight
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = wt)) +
  geom_point() +
  WJP_theme(family = "Inter Tight")


# Report style: dark text, horizontal grid only, minimal base theme
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = wt)) +
  geom_point() +
  WJP_theme(text_colour = "#1A1A1A", grid = "y",
            base_theme = theme_minimal(base_size = 11))
